title: Can two different numbers have the same nearest ten?
description: Joseph watches two buses with different distance boards. The video picks a round number first and then two numbers close to it, for the nearest ten, hundred and thousand.
teaching_notes: One idea: pick the round number first, then two numbers close to it on each side. Many pairs are right; watch for pairs that only start the same.

source: Let Us Think 2, same nearest ten, hundred, thousand
video_script.why: The child can find a nearest number for one number, but not build two numbers that share it.
video_script.substitution: Choose the round number first, then one number a little below and one a little above, inside the limit for that place.
video_script.anchor: Joseph watching two buses at the Kochi bus stand
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu thinks two numbers that start the same share a nearest ten. Five thousand two hundred and sixty two and five thousand two hundred and sixty eight have different nearest tens.
video_script.payoff_line: stay close to the same round number

final_answer.value: (a) 3,142 and 3,138; (b) 4,520 and 4,480; (c) 6,100 and 5,800 (many answers are right)
final_answer.spoken: for example, three thousand one hundred and forty two and three thousand one hundred and thirty eight

maths_rules: open question: many pairs are right; these are reasoned samples
3,142 and 3,138: both within 2 of 3,140, so nearest ten 3,140 for both
4,520 and 4,480: both 20 from 4,500, so nearest hundred 4,500 for both
6,100 and 5,800: 100 above and 200 below 6,000, so nearest thousand 6,000 for both
limits: closer than 5 jumps for tens, 50 for hundreds, 500 for thousands
slip: 5,262 and 5,268 start the same, but their nearest tens are 5,260 and 5,270
video_script.design: Exercise, open question. Hint: pick the round number, then one number below and one above. The video gives reasoned samples and says other pairs are fine.

<bookmark mark='stay'/>Stay closer than five jumps for tens, fifty for hundreds, and five hundred for thousands. Try again with this.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Five thousand two hundred and sixty two and five thousand two hundred and sixty eight start the same. They share a nearest ten.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first is nearest to five thousand two hundred and sixty.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second is nearest to five thousand two hundred and seventy.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Starting the same is not enough, because the jumps decide.

beats.on_screen: round number 3,140 with 3,142 two jumps above and 3,138 two jumps below
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Stay close to the same round number, one number below it and one above it.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>For the nearest ten, choose three thousand one hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Three thousand one hundred and forty two is two jumps above it.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Three thousand one hundred and thirty eight is two jumps below it.
<bookmark mark='a4'/>Both are closer than five jumps. The nearest ten for both is three thousand one hundred and forty.

beats.on_screen: round number 4,500 with 4,520 twenty jumps above and 4,480 twenty jumps below
narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>For the nearest hundred, choose four thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Four thousand five hundred and twenty is twenty jumps above it.
<bookmark mark='b3'/>Four thousand four hundred and eighty is twenty jumps below it.
<bookmark mark='b4'/>Both are closer than fifty jumps. The nearest hundred for both is four thousand five hundred.

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>For the nearest thousand, choose six thousand.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>Six thousand one hundred is one hundred jumps above it.
<bookmark mark='c3'/>Five thousand eight hundred is two hundred jumps below it.
<bookmark mark='c4'/>Both are closer than five hundred jumps. The nearest thousand for both is six thousand.
<bookmark mark='c5'/>Many other pairs are right too.

<bookmark mark='own'/>Your own pair may differ from ours, and it can still be right.
